PAYDAR / PRIVACY

Privacy by design.

Android application

The beta stores checks, imported records, subscription entries, transaction receipts, recovery drafts, and reminder settings in the app's private local database. The application uses internet access for optional Google sign-in through Firebase Authentication. Google and Firebase process account identifiers, name, email and authentication information. Payment records are not uploaded or synced. Signing out does not erase this device's records; all accounts on this app installation share the same local storage.

Camera access is used only to decode a QR code after you start a scan. SMS access is optional. If granted, PayDar reviews up to 1,000 recent inbox messages locally, extracts supported merchant, amount, and date fields, and does not save raw message bodies. You can paste a single message instead.

Payment notification capture is optional and starts disabled. Android notification access can expose notifications from all apps. PayDar processes only the payment app packages you select and saves extracted receipt fields, not raw notification bodies. Disable capture or revoke Android notification access at any time. Exporting transactions writes payment details to the file location you select.

Sharing a recovery draft or opening an official support page is an action you start. The receiving app or site then handles that information under its own privacy policy.

Delete your cloud account from Account after confirming your Google identity. Local records are deleted separately using Delete local PayDar data. No advertising or analytics SDK is included.

Marketing website

This website is a hosted product presentation. Its browser demonstration uses the information you enter in the current page only and does not initiate a payment. The download link points to the beta build packaged with this project.

Deletion

Use the app's Account section to delete local PayDar records and disable transaction capture and reminders. Files you previously shared to another application are controlled by that application.

Questions

Before production release, publish a named data controller, support contact, retention schedule, and store-ready privacy policy that matches the final permissions and integrations.
